name: 8 Coil Shakti 'as seen on TV': chirp both sides, then amygdala left
origin: Todd Murphy (8 Coil Shakti software); signal templates licensed from Persinger & Koren
summary: Todd Murphy's starred 'as seen on TV' two-phase session for the 8 Coil Shakti: the modulated 40 Hz chirp over both temporal lobes for 20 min, then amygdala burst-firing over the left temporal lobe for 20 min (the 40-min run most users prefer, Murphy says). Murphy calls it the design that 'comes closest to the sessions used in the God Helmet experiments' (on two stereo channels) and links its after-effects to the left amygdala.
notes: Coils as in the photos on the vendor's output pages for the left-ending sessions: six on the left and two on the right ('The left side has four coils from the left channel, and two coils from the right channel. The right side has two coils from the right stereo channel.'). The four left-channel coils form a cross over the left temporal lobe (FT7 front, C5 top, TP7 back, T9 bottom; CH1-4); the two right-channel coils on the left sit inside that cross, above-front and below-back of its centre (FTT7h and TTP9h; CH5-6), and the two on the right form the same diagonal pair over the right temporal lobe (FTT8h and TTP10h; CH7-8). The 10-5 sites are read from the photos and are an inference. Phase 1 (20 min) drives the four right-channel coils together (the right channel over both sides); phase 2 (20 min, abrupt switch) drives the four left-channel coils (the left channel over the left side only). There is no rotation, as on the two-channel Shakti. Polarity: Murphy's software demo video says of this session that 'all of the coils on the left side of the head are positive' (the package includes four extra positive coils for it), so all six left coils run as is; on the right the upper-front coil (FTT8h) runs as is and the lower-back coil (TTP10h) reversed (weight -1), as in the page's photo of the right side. The page's photo of the left side shows a mix instead (left channel: top and front -, back and bottom +; right channel: upper-front +, lower-back -); murphy-shakti8-twophase-family-hippbi-amyl and -mod40bi-amyl follow those photos. Durations: the output pages and Murphy's demo video offer 40- and 60-min runs, and the video says 'most users seem to prefer the 40-minute session, 20 minutes of each of the signals seems to be enough' (in agreement, Murphy says, with some of the laboratory work); this file is that 40-min run. The 60-min run is presumably 30 + 30 min (not stated). The rotating Shiva God Helmet versions of this design are murphy-gh-chirpbi-amyl-40min and -60min. The 'modulated 40 Hz chirp' is proprietary (Murphy relates it to the frequency-modulated Thomas pattern and describes it as the modulated 40 Hz signal with gaps that get longer, amplitude and gaps varied by a Fibonacci constant); it is approximated by a sweep slowing from 40 to 6 Hz (the end frequency is a choice), 837 points at 3 ms (2.5 s) once every 4 s, after the published FM pattern (837 points at 1 ms every 4 s; Tiller & Persinger 2002 and the Shakti use 3-ms points). The 40 Hz phase modulation and the Fibonacci amplitude changes are not reproduced. The amygdala 'burstx' signal is proprietary; it is approximated by the built-in accelerating burst (6 to 30 Hz) of 230 points at the standard 3-ms points (0.69 s, after the published 230-point burst-firing pattern), then the standard 4-s silence. Vendor cautions: the chirp can be 'very unpleasant over the right side'; if phase 1 gets too uncomfortable, press Skip to go to phase 2, though finishing the session is advised. First test the amygdala signal on each side with 10-min test sessions. For the God Helmet version of this design Murphy advises: if anger appears during or after the session, don't use it again; not for people prone to anger. The effects are vendor claims backed only by user reports. Independent double-blind tests found no field effect (Granqvist 2005; Gendle & McGrath 2012, the latter with the 8 Coil Shakti amygdala signal). Not for anyone with epilepsy or a seizure history, a psychiatric condition or medication, migraine or brain injury, or on drugs; this is not a treatment. Stop at once on fear or distress. Revised after a re-check of the vendor's two-phase pages (2026): 20 + 20 min instead of 30 + 30, eight separate coils as on the output pages instead of six with two shared between the phases, and polarity from Murphy's demo video and the page's photo of the right side instead of the general coil chart. Still approximate: the coil sites and both signal templates.
setting: Darkness and acoustic silence ('not just quiet'), at night; eyes closed or blindfolded; relax without meditating or falling asleep. A helper can press Skip or Stop so you stay in the dark. The vendor: 'You don't have to use sensory deprivation if you're looking for after-effects.'
schedule: Vendor: while trying sessions out, at most every 72 h; once you settle on a session, once a week; never on consecutive days. For sessions of an hour or more (the 60-min run) the demo video and the safety pages say once every 3 weeks (one week if the session had no effect), but the vendor's 60-minute page exempts two-phase sessions from that rule.
